core_obligations: Present the profinite space (proof lines 1103-1107): write T as the limit of an inverse system of finite discrete spaces T_i over a directed set and set Z_i equal to the image of T in the product of the components of X with T_i, a closed subset.

Build the pieces (proof lines 1107-1117): the product X x T_i is the spectrum of the product A_i of copies of A indexed by T_i, with A -> A_i a local isomorphism; the construction lemma applied to the closed subset Z_i of the components gives a surjective ind-Zariski map A_i -> B_i whose spectrum is the part of X x T_i lying over Z_i.

Take the limit (proof lines 1117-1132): the transition maps induce compatible maps B_{i'} -> B_i, so the colimit B of the B_i is ind-Zariski over A; since T is the limit of the Z_i, the spectrum of B is the fibre product of X with T over the components of X, and by the component computation T is the space of connected components of Spec(B), as required.
proof_roadmap: Present the profinite space as a limit of finite discrete spaces and cut out the corresponding closed subsets of the components.
For each index build an ind-Zariski quotient realizing that closed subset.
Pass to the colimit and identify the components.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a ring A and a continuous map from a profinite space T to the space of connected components of Spec(A) there is an ind-Zariski ring map A -> B whose spectrum is the fibre product of Spec(A) with T over the components, with T the space of connected components of Spec(B) (statement lines 1097-1110). The proof (proof lines 1112-1139) writes T as a limit of finite discrete spaces, realizes each closed piece by an ind-Zariski quotient via the construction lemma, and passes to the colimit. H2: a three-step construction with four inputs, written out in full.
